instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines “lobbying” as attempting to influence legislative or administrative action by oral or written communication and explicitly includes time spent preparing for such communication, appearances at public hearings or meetings, and service on a committee in which such preparation or communication occurs.

A “lobbyist” is defined as an individual employed by or receiving economic consideration from a principal whose duties include lobbying, with a 5-days-per-reporting-period test if duties are not exclusively lobbying.

When an individual’s duties are not limited exclusively to lobbying, the statute applies a quantitative threshold—lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period—to determine whether the person is a lobbyist.

Lobbying includes communications intended to influence administrative action with an “agency official,” and “agency” is defined broadly as state government boards, commissions, departments, offices, etc.

“Agency official” includes an agency member, officer, employee, or consultant who participates in administrative action, and lobbying is defined as communication with an agency official to influence legislative or administrative action.

“Legislative action” expressly includes the governor’s approval or veto of bills and development of proposals for introduction in the legislature, and lobbying covers attempts to influence legislative action via communication with covered officials.

The definition of “agency” encompasses boards, commissions, councils, committees, and various authorities in state government (excluding only legislative councils/committees), covering independent agencies and commissions.
“Legislative action” includes actions by the legislature and its committees, and “lobbying” includes attempts to influence legislative action by communication with covered officials.

Lobbying is defined as communication with a “legislative employee,” and “legislative employee” is defined to include members/officers of the legislature and specified legislative employees/service agency staff.
The statute defines “elective state official” and includes such officials as covered targets for lobbying communications in the definition of lobbying.
The lobbying definition covers communications with “agency officials” and “legislative employees,” both of which include employees (and certain consultants) of state agencies or the legislature.
